title: Tornado
summary: Watch: be ready. Warning: take shelter now in the lowest interior room, away from windows. Mobile homes are not safe.

sources.title: WTVR: Several tornadoes confirmed across central Virginia (Sept 18, 2018)

blocks.text: Tornadoes happen in Henrico. On September 17, 2018, an EF-1 tornado with 90 to 95 mph winds crossed from Richmond into the Tuckahoe area, uprooting trees onto houses and tearing air-conditioning units off a church roof.

rows: Stay near a sturdy building or shelter, and keep watching alerts
A tornado has been sighted or shown on radar

items: Learn the signs: a rotating, funnel-shaped cloud, an approaching cloud of debris, or a loud roar.
Sign up for warnings: Emergency Alert System, NOAA Weather Radio, local alerts.
Pick your shelter now. Best: a FEMA-criteria safe room or ICC 500 storm shelter. Next best: a small interior windowless room, or the lowest level of a sturdy building (basement, cellar).
Stock supplies for staying at home: food, water, medicine.
Go to your shelter **right away**: basement or lowest level. No basement? An inside closet or hallway.
Stay away from **corners, windows, doors and outer walls**. Never open windows.
Cover your head and neck with your arms. Put blankets or furniture over you.

blocks.text: **Mobile or manufactured home: leave immediately** for the closest sturdy building or shelter. Mobile homes are not safe in a tornado.
In a car, or caught outside

items: No option is truly safe. If you have no shelter, get into a vehicle and buckle your seat belt, head below the windows, covered by your hands. Or, if you can get noticeably lower than the road, lie in a ditch or low area with your head covered.
**Don't shelter under an overpass or bridge.** It offers little protection from debris and creates traffic hazards.
Keep watching alerts and follow officials.
Stay away from downed power lines and broken utility lines.
Text instead of calling. Save calls for emergencies.
Wear thick-soled shoes, long pants and work gloves for cleanup. Use a mask around mold or debris.
